scenario.title: Prime Way Care Ltd v The Mayor and Burgesses of the London Borough of Southwark
scenario.description: This judgment determines an application by Prime Way for specific disclosure brought against Southwark. Prime Way has brought a challenge under the Procurement Act 2023 to the procurement by Southwark for the establishment of a multi-lot framework agreement relating to Adult Home Care Services. The evaluation process was flawed, with Southwark relying on ex post facto explanations and not disclosing primary documents. The claimant alleges that the defendant breached Section 12 of the Procurement Act 2023, specifically Transparency and Integrity, by evaluating the claimant's response against standard practice and measurable outcomes benchmarks absent from the published Procurement Selection Questionnaire (PSQ). The evaluation panel followed the standard evaluator guidance issued to all officers involved in this procurement, ensuring consistency and adherence to the published scoring criteria. The court has ordered specific disclosure of contemporaneous records of the evaluation of the claimant's response to question 22(ii) of the PSQ.
scenario.contracting_authority_name: The Mayor and Burgesses of the London Borough of Southwark

interests: Compliance & Legality: Act lawfully within vires and defend the procurement decision
Protection of Public Funds: Avoid significant delay costs and ensure value for money is delivered
Continuity of Service / Delivery: Deliver Adult Home Care Services promptly to vulnerable adults in Southwark
Reputation & Public Accountability: Maintain public confidence as a competent, fair and professional buyer
goals: Defend the procurement decision and maintain transparency throughout the process
ca_pre_negotiation.batna: Defend the decision in the TCC — costly (£50k+) and slow (6-12 months), with a real risk of automatic suspension.
ca_pre_negotiation.opening_position: The evaluation panel followed standard evaluator guidance, ensuring consistency and adherence to published scoring criteria

interests: Commercial Loss & Recovery: A significant investment of time and resource was made in this bid, which may have been wasted due to Southwark's evaluation flaws.
Fairness & Transparency: The lack of transparency and consistency in the evaluation process undermines our confidence in the fairness of the outcome.
Protection of Reputation: Our reputation as a capable bidder is at risk if we are seen as having lost due to poor performance or capability, rather than procedural issues.
goals: Force Southwark to re-evaluate our bid
Obtain damages for any financial losses incurred
bidder_pre_negotiation.batna: Pursue a damages claim in the TCC — costly (£50k-£100k in legal fees) for a business our size, slow, and the outcome is uncertain.
bidder_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We request that Southwark provide detailed feedback on their evaluation process, including contemporaneous records of the evaluation of our response to question 22(ii) of the PSQ.
legal_basis: Section 12 of the Procurement Act 2023: Transparency and Integrity

messages.message: I acknowledge Prime Way Care Ltd's concerns regarding transparency and integrity in our procurement process for Adult Home Care Services. I would like to clarify whether the specific disclosure ordered by the court relates only to question 22(ii) of the PSQ, or if it encompasses other aspects of the evaluation process. Furthermore, I'd appreciate more information on how Prime Way believes we breached Section 12 of the Procurement Act 2023, specifically in relation to transparency and integrity.

I appreciate your clarification request regarding the scope of disclosure ordered by the court. However, I must express my concern that your response does not directly address the substance of Prime Way's allegations. Specifically, we believe that the evaluation panel did rely on ex post facto explanations and failed to disclose primary documents as required by Section 12 of the Procurement Act 2023. I would like to request more information about how the standard evaluator guidance issued to all officers involved in this procurement ensured consistency and adherence to the published scoring criteria, particularly with regards to question 22(ii) of the PSQ. Furthermore, we believe that the court's order for specific disclosure implies a level of transparency that was not initially provided by Southwark.

I understand Prime Way's concerns regarding transparency and integrity in our procurement process for Adult Home Care Services. To address these concerns, I am willing to provide additional feedback on how the evaluation panel followed the standard evaluator guidance issued to all officers involved in this procurement, ensuring consistency and adherence to the published scoring criteria. Specifically, we can share the contemporaneous records of the evaluation of Prime Way's response to question 22(ii) of the PSQ, as ordered by the court. This will provide further transparency into our evaluation process.
messages.concession_made: Providing additional feedback on the evaluation panel's adherence to published scoring criteria

messages.message: While I appreciate your offer to provide additional feedback on how the evaluation panel followed the standard evaluator guidance, I remain concerned that this does not directly address the issue of primary documents being withheld. Specifically, can you confirm whether the contemporaneous records of the evaluation of Prime Way's response to question 22(ii) of the PSQ will include any notes or communications regarding the scoring discrepancy between our bid and the winning bidder? Furthermore, I would like to request that these records be made available in a format that is easily accessible and understandable. If this can be done, it may help to alleviate some of Prime Way's concerns regarding transparency and integrity in the procurement process.

applicable_provisions: Section 12 of the Procurement Act 2023, specifically Transparency and Integrity
compliance_checks.reasoning: The prima facie case is met as Prime Way has shown a concern about transparency and integrity in Southwark's procurement process. The specificity test is also met as the disclosure sought relates to question 22(ii) of the PSQ, which is directly connected to the claimant's articulated concern. However, the proportionality test requires further consideration as the scope of disclosure ordered by the court is not explicitly stated. To balance this, I will recommend a continuation of negotiation to clarify the scope and ensure that only relevant information is disclosed.

applicable_provisions: Section 12 of the Procurement Act 2023 (Transparency and Integrity)
compliance_checks.reasoning: Prime Way has shown a prima facie case that there may be something wrong with the evaluation, specifically regarding transparency and integrity. The claimant alleges that Southwark breached Section 12 by evaluating their response against standard practice and measurable outcomes benchmarks absent from the published PSQ. This concern is specific to the scoring discrepancy between Prime Way's bid and the winning bidder, which is a real, articulated issue in dispute. The request for disclosure of contemporaneous records of the evaluation of question 22(ii) of the PSQ, including any notes or communications regarding the scoring discrepancy, meets the specificity test. However, the burden of disclosing these records in an easily accessible and understandable format may be proportionate to the evidential value to the actual dispute. Confidentiality safeguards are not explicitly mentioned, but it is assumed that measures will be taken to protect commercially sensitive material.

ca_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The final outcome was slightly unfavourable, but it avoided the significant costs and risks associated with a lengthy court battle. The BATNA of defending in TCC court would have cost £50k+ and taken 6-12 months.
ca_win_statement.win_statement: We successfully negotiated to limit the scope of disclosure ordered by the court, while still providing additional transparency into our evaluation process. This outcome demonstrates our commitment to openness and accountability in public procurement.
what_was_achieved: Provided additional feedback on how the evaluation panel followed standard evaluator guidance
Shared contemporaneous records of the evaluation of Prime Way's response to question 22(ii) of the PSQ
what_was_conceded: Specific disclosure of contemporaneous records was ordered by the court, which may have been avoided with more transparency during the procurement process
Limited scope of disclosure negotiated, but still required to provide additional information

bidder_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The negotiation outcome is slightly favourable relative to pursuing damages or formal TCC proceedings, as we have achieved some level of transparency and accountability from the contracting authority. However, it falls short in addressing the core issue of primary documents being withheld.
bidder_win_statement.win_statement: We successfully negotiated for specific disclosure of contemporaneous records of the evaluation process, which will provide further insight into the procurement decisions made by Southwark. This outcome is a partial victory for Prime Way Care Ltd, as we have managed to expose some of the flaws in the procurement process.
what_was_achieved: Specific disclosure of contemporaneous records of the evaluation of our response to question 22(ii) of the PSQ
Additional feedback on how the evaluation panel followed standard evaluator guidance
what_was_conceded: The contracting authority did not directly address the issue of primary documents being withheld, and no confirmation was provided regarding notes or communications about scoring discrepancies between our bid and the winning bidder.

key_sticking_points: Transparency and integrity in the procurement process
Disclosure of primary documents and contemporaneous records
Scoring discrepancy between Prime Way's bid and the winning bidder
summary.concessions_summary: The Contracting Authority made two concessions: (1) providing additional feedback on how the evaluation panel followed the standard evaluator guidance, and (2) offering to disclose contemporaneous records of the evaluation of question 22(ii) of the PSQ.
summary.court_reasoning_summary: The Court assessed each round based on three criteria: process_followed, manifest_error, and proportionality. In Round 1, the Court recommended continuing negotiation due to unclear scope of disclosure. In Round 2, the Court ordered disclosure after finding a prima facie case for transparency and integrity issues, with specific concerns about scoring discrepancies.
summary.likely_next_steps: The likely next step is that the Contracting Authority will disclose the contemporaneous records of the evaluation of question 22(ii) of the PSQ, including any notes or communications regarding the scoring discrepancy. This may alleviate some of Prime Way's concerns and potentially lead to a settlement or re-evaluation of the procurement process.
summary.plain_english_summary: The negotiation centered around transparency and integrity issues in Southwark's procurement process for Adult Home Care Services. The Contracting Authority made concessions, but the Aggrieved Bidder remained concerned about primary documents being withheld. The Court ultimately ordered disclosure of contemporaneous records to address these concerns.
